title: Build an autonomously reproducing cell from defined components

concept.text: The innovation would be to assemble a cell from specified nonliving components that can sustain its own essential machinery and reproduce across generations. Its genome, protein-making machinery, metabolism and surrounding membrane would work together: the cell would take up nutrients, renew its working parts, grow, divide and transmit genetic information to offspring. Autonomy here permits a supplied nutrient environment; it requires the cell to maintain the machinery that turns those nutrients into continued cellular activity.

The defining advance is sustained integration. Copying DNA, producing proteins or dividing a membrane compartment demonstrates important parts of the problem, but those functions must support one another through successive generations. A synthetic genome operating inside an existing recipient cell is a different achievement because the recipient supplies an already functioning cellular system. Similarly, a constructed vesicle that repeatedly receives replacement ribosomes and enzymes has not yet demonstrated the stronger autonomy proposed here.

significance.text: If achieved, this would make a living, reproducing and potentially evolvable cellular system something researchers could construct and vary component by component. Knowing the identity and concentration of the starting components would allow unusually controlled experiments on how inheritance, metabolism, membrane behavior and reproduction depend on one another. Successful construction would directly establish that the specified components and processes are sufficient for cellular reproduction under the demonstrated conditions.

Synthesis: Such a result would not by itself identify a uniquely minimal cell, a universal recipe for life or the historical route by which life first arose. Multiple cellular designs could satisfy the same functional requirements, and a design assembled using sophisticated modern biochemical components would not establish that those components could have formed under early-Earth conditions. Its immediate significance would be experimental control over a sufficient cellular system; broader conclusions would require additional comparisons and evidence.

Biological manufacturing is a possible downstream application. Engineered synthetic cells might eventually produce chemicals, fuels or medicines, but the supplied reporting presents these as future possibilities and explicitly says SpudCells cannot yet perform that manufacturing role. Achieving autonomous reproduction would still leave substantial work on useful output, reliability and operating conditions before such platforms became practical.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a complete reproduction cycle in which the system renews its essential machinery instead of progressively exhausting or diluting the machinery supplied at assembly. The SpudCell preprint makes this distinction concrete: its synthetic cells have very limited metabolism and cannot make ribosomes, while feeder liposomes supply enzymes, protein-making machinery, small molecules and lipids. Repeated cycles supported by those inputs demonstrate substantial functional integration, but leave the machinery-renewal problem unresolved.

Engineering synthesis: Closing that gap requires coordinated production and assembly of the components needed for gene expression, including ribosomes, together with sufficient energy and precursor supply. Genome copying, membrane growth and division must proceed at compatible rates, and offspring must inherit enough genome and working machinery to continue the cycle. These are coupled constraints: making more membrane is insufficient if genetic material or essential components fail to reach viable offspring, and copying a genome is insufficient if its instructions cannot replenish the machinery that reads it.

Division and evolutionary behavior present additional integration barriers. In the supplied SpudCell evidence, the five-generation experiment used mechanical division; a separate experiment linked division to expressed membrane proteins but required externally added division reagents. The reported selection experiment also began with an artificially introduced beneficial promoter variant. These results motivate distinct remaining demonstrations: division sustained by the constructed cell's own processes, and adaptation involving newly arising heritable variation rather than selection only among variants supplied by researchers.

current_state.text: Gaut et al., in the preprint “A Chemically Defined Synthetic Cell Capable Of Growth And Replication,” posted July 2, 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.07.01.735724, report five generations of a synthetic cell cycle combining genetically encoded feeding and growth, DNA replication and mechanical division. This is a reported advance in integrating cellular functions across repeated cycles. The five-generation result should not be interpreted as five generations of autonomous division.

The feeder liposomes in those experiments contain no DNA but replenish enzymes and small molecules needed for the system, including RNA polymerase, the Phi29 DNA-replication enzyme and the PURE protein-synthesis system. They also supply ribosomes and lipids. The authors explicitly identify the inability to make ribosomes and the cells' limited metabolism as remaining limitations. Continued reproduction under this feeding regime therefore does not establish that the cells synthesize and renew all of their essential machinery.

Separately, the preprint reports coupling feeding, DNA replication and division through expressed membrane proteins, with externally supplied streptavidin and antibody linkers used to induce division. This experiment extends the connection between genetic expression and membrane behavior, but must be distinguished from the mechanically divided five-generation series. The reported selection experiment likewise demonstrates a narrower result than spontaneous adaptive evolution: researchers introduced a beneficial promoter variant and then observed selection involving that variant.

These SpudCell findings are unreviewed reported results. According to the supplied review, the retained landing page verifies the paper's identity and posting date, and the retained PDF extracts permit inspection of substantial results and methods. Both PDF extracts nevertheless end during Methods section 21 on page 41; some numerical extraction is damaged, and figures and supplementary data were not visually inspected. This supports describing what the authors report while leaving a full methodological assessment incomplete. The earlier research note's account of a 403 response does not describe the evidence subsequently available to the review.

Tina Hesman Saey's July 17, 2026 Science News report also describes SpudCells' dependence on supplied protein-making machinery and chemical assistance. It provides a separate journalistic account consistent with those limitations, rather than independent experimental replication. The retained article records an August 17 correction, so the supplied review concerns that updated version and does not establish the exact wording of the original July publication.

The earlier research also attributes “A synthetic cell with integrated DNA self-replication and lipid biosynthesis,” DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-69531-9, to Restrepo Sierra et al., with a February 13, 2026 publication date. It describes partial-genome expression, DNA replication and membrane synthesis using supplied PURE machinery. However, the supplied review found only a cookie-access notice in the retained PubMed content, with no article identity, abstract or figure caption available to substantiate those details. The attribution, date and scientific description therefore remain unverified within this record; the access limitation is not evidence that the paper or its reported result is false.

Evidence boundary: The supplied material establishes dated reports and their stated limitations, but contains no completed freshness search establishing the latest field-wide position as of November 1, 2026. It therefore does not justify declaring these the latest results or concluding that no other group had achieved a stronger result by that date. The documented SpudCell experiments themselves do not complete the autonomous-cell milestone defined here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Assemble a cell from an explicitly specified set of nonliving components and show that it takes up supplied nutrients, synthesizes and renews its essential machinery, grows, divides repeatedly and passes its genome to viable offspring. Document the initial components, the environment and every subsequent input so that the contribution of the constructed system can be distinguished from external support. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Defined nonliving components produce reproducing cells with viable offspring

completion_criteria.text: Proposed autonomy test: Continue reproduction across enough generations, with appropriate measurements of component replacement, to distinguish ongoing synthesis from persistence of initially supplied machinery. No fixed generation count is established by the supplied evidence. Nutrient provision is compatible with this proposal, but continued replenishment of essential enzymes, ribosomes or other cellular machinery would not satisfy its autonomy requirement. The experiment should also show how division is sustained without repeated mechanical intervention or externally supplied division machinery.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduction persists through machinery renewal without external machinery replenishment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed inheritance and adaptation test: Track genome transmission and reproductive competence across offspring, and demonstrate a heritable functional change under a defined selective condition. Distinguish selection among deliberately introduced variants from adaptation involving newly arising heritable variation. The latter would provide stronger evidence that the constructed system supports evolutionary change beyond the variants chosen at assembly.
completion_criteria.label: Offspring inherit genomes and functional change under defined selection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements: Independent groups should reproduce the central construction and sustained reproduction result, with controls excluding carryover of living cells. Reports should specify nutrient dependence, environmental requirements, duration, generation count and failure conditions. Finite experiments would establish reproduction and adaptation across the tested conditions; they would not establish literal universality, indefinite persistence or independence from every environmental resource.
completion_criteria.label: Independent groups reproduce construction and sustained reproduction with stated limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIO-02, “Demonstrate a plausible chemical transition from nonlife to evolution,” shares the interest in constructing systems capable of inheritance and evolutionary change. BIO-01 asks whether specified components can sustain an autonomous cell; BIO-02 additionally asks whether a chemically plausible route can lead from nonlife to evolution. A successful BIO-01 construction using modern biochemical machinery would not automatically resolve that origin-of-life requirement.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-03, “Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts,” and BIO-14, “Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins,” could benefit from a controlled synthetic cellular platform. Such a platform could support direct perturbation experiments with known components, but explaining behavior in one constructed cell would not establish predictive generality across biological contexts or resolve functions throughout natural genomes.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” concerns a predictive model, whereas BIO-01 concerns a physical reproducing system. They could support one another through model-guided construction and experimental tests. BIO-10, “Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale,” supplies a complementary measurement goal: observing molecular processes could help determine whether a constructed cell actually renews its machinery and coordinates reproduction.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-05, “Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes,” could supply useful catalytic components for synthetic metabolism. BIO-01 would still require those enzymes to function within a coordinated, self-maintaining cellular cycle. BIO-15, “Deliver programmable genome editors selectively to diverse cells in the body,” overlaps through genome manipulation, but its defining challenge is selective delivery in an organism rather than construction of a reproducing cell from components.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-11, “Reconstruct the major steps in the origin of eukaryotic cells,” and BIO-12, “Explain how biological homochirality could emerge and persist,” address distinct historical and mechanistic questions about life's organization. Constructed cells might become experimental tools for investigating aspects of those questions, but autonomous reproduction alone would not explain eukaryotic origins or the emergence and persistence of molecular handedness.

brief.title: Cells built from parts that reproduce on their own
possible: Researchers could build a reproducing cell from known nonliving ingredients and change its parts to see how life works. Supplied with nutrients, it would replace its own working machinery, grow, divide and pass DNA—the molecule carrying genetic instructions—to offspring that could continue the cycle.
why: This would let scientists test how inheritance, energy use and reproduction depend on one another in a system whose starting ingredients they know. Successful construction would establish which components are enough to sustain cellular reproduction under the tested conditions.

sources.who: Ana María Restrepo Sierra and collaborators
sources.showed: They combined protein production, DNA copying and membrane production inside fatty membrane bubbles. The system used supplied protein-making machinery.
sources.quote: The synthetic genome encodes six proteins, and its compartmentalized expression produces active liposomes with distinct phenotypes demonstrating successful module integration.
sources.cited_for: Essential cellular processes can operate together inside a constructed compartment.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish repeated reproduction with renewal of all essential machinery.

sources.who: Nathaniel J. Gaut and collaborators at the University of Minnesota
sources.showed: Their SpudCells linked genetic instructions to feeding, growth and division. They also demonstrated selection favoring a deliberately introduced genetic variant. These results are a preprint and have not undergone peer review.
sources.quote: We demonstrated five generations of the overall cell cycle including DNA replication, feeding, and growth (Figure 3), first tested with mechanical division - to ensure high efficiency of replication.
sources.cited_for: Constructed cells can combine several essential functions across repeated cycles.
sources.not_established: The cells still receive replacement machinery, including ribosomes, the structures that make proteins, and external help with division.

sources.showed: Her reporting describes SpudCells’ dependence on supplied protein-making machinery and chemical help with growth and division.
sources.quote: To function, they require researchers to feed them bubbles packed full of protein-building machinery and raw materials.
sources.cited_for: The reported cell cycles depend on substantial external support.
sources.not_established: This reporting provides no independent experimental reproduction of the results.

shown: Gaut and colleagues report SpudCells continuing through five generations with mechanical division. A separate experiment connected division to proteins made inside the cells, but required added chemicals to trigger it.
missing: The cells would need to make and replace their essential machinery while reproduction continues.
Growth, DNA copying and division would need to stay coordinated so offspring inherit enough working parts to reproduce.
The system would need to sustain division without repeated mechanical intervention or externally supplied division machinery.
Adaptation from newly arising inherited changes and independent reproduction of the complete construction remain to be demonstrated.

milestones.label: Known nonliving ingredients yield reproducing cells and viable offspring
milestones.explanation: Specified nonliving ingredients would have to yield cells that feed, renew their machinery, grow, divide and pass DNA to viable offspring, with all inputs accounted for. This would establish a complete constructed reproduction cycle.

milestones.label: Reproduction continues as cells replace their own machinery
milestones.explanation: Reproduction would have to outlast the starting machinery, with measured replacement and division sustained without outside machinery or repeated mechanical help. This would distinguish self-maintenance from dependence on supplied parts.

milestones.label: Offspring inherit genetic instructions and useful changes
milestones.explanation: Offspring would have to inherit DNA, reproduce and retain a functional change under a defined condition favoring it. Changes arising within the system would provide stronger evidence of evolution than researcher-supplied variants.

milestones.label: Independent groups reproduce construction and sustained reproduction
milestones.explanation: Independent groups would have to repeat construction and sustained reproduction, exclude contamination by living cells and state operating limits. This would establish reproducibility within the tested conditions.

uncertain: How many generations, and which measurements of machinery replacement, would convincingly establish self-maintenance?
Can cells produce and assemble their own protein-making machinery while meeting the energy demands of continued reproduction?

page.title: Autonomously reproducing bottom-up synthetic cells
page.definition: Cells assembled from defined nonliving components renew their molecular machinery and repeatedly grow, copy their genomes and divide into reproducing offspring. Nutrients may be supplied; ribosomes, the machines that make proteins, and other essential machinery are regenerated internally.

goal.need: The genome-minimized bacterium JCVI-syn3.0 still contained genes with unknown biological functions in its report published on 25 March 2016, as quantified below. Constructing a reproducing cell from specified components would test sufficient combinations of components and permit analysis of the minimal functional units of cellular processes.

figures.note: These are the classifications reported in 2016.

completion.title: A synthetic cell completes ≥10 coordinated growth–division cycles with internal ribosome regeneration.
completion.criterion: A cell assembled from nonliving molecular components completes at least 10 continuous, coordinated growth–division cycles with endogenous, genome-encoded ribosome regeneration replacing the external cell-free expression system. Replenishing ribosomes between cycles does not satisfy this target.
completion.set_by: SynCell Asia Initiative, AutoCell reproduction target, published in the Chinese Academy of Sciences' announcement on 28 May 2026.
completion.threshold_quote: AutoCell to complete ≥10 continuous, coordinated growth-division cycles
completion.basis: This is the reproduction objective within the AutoCell roadmap, rather than a field-wide certification standard. It pairs a cycle count with replacement of externally supplied expression machinery. Evolution and community formation are additional roadmap objectives. SpudCell's developer still reports supplied ribosomes and external division reagents, so its reported reproduction does not establish this target.

milestones.title: DNA replicates inside an encapsulated cell-free system.
milestones.criterion: DNA replicates inside an encapsulated cell-free system. On 13 February 2026, Restrepo Sierra and colleagues reported a six-gene genome coupling DNA replication and lipid synthesis inside liposomes using supplied PURE, a mixture of purified gene-expression components. Their module-activity comparison used three biological replicates. This demonstrates the component milestone, without machinery renewal or autonomous cellular reproduction.
milestones.threshold_quote: Accomplish DNA replication in an encapsulated cell-free system

milestones.title: Synthetic translation machinery produces functional ribosomes and translation components.
milestones.criterion: Ribosomes produce components that assemble into functional ribosomes, together with the remaining translation apparatus. On 8 January 2025, Kosaka and colleagues reported functional new ribosomal subunits in E. coli extracts; Figure 5B used three biological replicates. Some ribosomal proteins came from the starting machinery. Continuous ribosome self-renewal was not demonstrated.

milestones.title: A synthetic compartment divides autonomously with machinery that segregates its DNA.
milestones.criterion: A synthetic cellular compartment divides autonomously with machinery that segregates DNA. SpudCell division still requires externally supplied streptavidin and linker proteins. Its developer reports complete genomes in approximately 30% of daughter cells after five generations, without a sample size on the page. These developer-reported results are not peer reviewed and do not establish autonomous genome segregation.
milestones.set_by: Build-a-Cell, 2024 roadmap, Box 2, step 4b, under “Achieve autonomous division of”.

milestones.title: A cell-free gene-expression system regenerates its machinery through repeated operating cycles.
milestones.criterion: A cell-free system repeatedly regenerates its transcription and translation machinery; the roadmap specifies no cycle count. On 22 May 2026, Mottaghi and Maerkl reported simultaneous synthesis of 36 non-ribosome PURE proteins and reconstitution of protein expression after purification; functional assays used two technical replicates. This is partial progress: supplied ribosomes and external purification remain.

not_found: The SynCell Asia journal article's full text was inaccessible; its numerical reproduction target was available in the Chinese Academy of Sciences' announcement.
The SpudCell bioRxiv manuscript returned HTTP 403, and the developer-hosted PDF exceeded the retrieval limit.
No cycle count or quantitative acceptance threshold was found for the four Build-a-Cell component milestones.
No independently replicated demonstration meeting the AutoCell reproduction target was found.

results.finding: Encapsulated DNA replication and lipid synthesis were jointly active in 2.9% of liposomes across eight biological replicates.
results.detail: The genome and supplied PURE expression system were encapsulated in liposomes. The system did not demonstrate machinery renewal or autonomous reproduction.

results.finding: Encapsulated DNA replicated over 5 generations; 3 independently prepared liposome samples.
results.detail: The liposomes contained a PURE expression system and Phi29 replication machinery. Division between generations was mechanical.
results.quote: Newly synthesized DNA was detected in cells after each generation.

results.finding: Daughter fractions contained all plasmids of a 90 kbp genome; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Division required externally supplied streptavidin and linker. The source reports no DNA segregation mechanism, and detection in the daughter fraction does not establish complete genomes in individual daughters.
results.quote:
Each of the plasmids 
comprising the 90kbp genome was detected in the daughter cell fraction that went through DNA 
replication, feeding and division (Figure 6r).

results.finding: SpudCells replicate their DNA; sample size and replication count not reported.
results.detail: The membrane compartments contain DNA and use externally supplied protein-building machinery.
results.quote:
unveiled SpudCells, synthetic cells
that can replicate their DNA and divide multiple times.

results.finding: About 30% of SpudCells inherited the complete genome after five generations; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Researchers chemically coax division, and the cells lack a cytoskeleton to guide genome segregation.
results.quote:
Without a cytoskeleton to guide division only about 30 percent of SpudCells
inherited the full seven-piece genome
after five generations, Adamala and colleagues reported in their manuscript, which posted to bioRxiv.org the day after the announcement and has yet to undergo peer review.

results.finding: Newly made ribosomal subunits formed functional ribosomes in E. coli extracts; three independent experiments, p = 1.0 × 10−5.
results.detail: Functional subunits were produced separately, purified and mixed. Some ribosomal proteins came from the starting machinery; regeneration of the remaining translation apparatus and continuous ribosome self-renewal were not demonstrated.
results.quote: We observed translational activity under the double-antibiotic condition only when we mixed the purified nascent artificial SSU and LSU.

results.finding: E. coli PURE system: 30 translation proteins self-regenerated simultaneously; n=6 DNA brush clusters.
results.detail: The system used supplied ribosomes and did not demonstrate assembly of new functional ribosomes. Initial translation factors and ribosome-associated contaminants also contributed to the reaction.
results.quote: The co-localization of genes, molecular machinery, messenger RNA and nascent proteins at the surface create sufficient conditions to catalyze the simultaneous self-regeneration of sub-groups up to all thirty translation proteins, as measured by total internal reflection fluorescence on the surface.

results.finding: In two chemostat replicates, in situ synthesis of 21 tRNAs supported steady-state sfGFP at 17 μg/ml.
results.detail: The system continuously synthesized functional tRNAs, but it did not demonstrate synthesis and assembly of functional ribosomes. Protein and ribosome components were replenished externally.
results.quote: By contrast, higher stable steady states of 10.5 μg/ml and 17 μg/ml sfGFP were obtained at 100 nM and 150 nM ltDNA input concentrations, respectively, achieving continuous in situ transcription of a full tRNA set alongside sustained long-term protein synthesis.

results.finding: ParMRC-containing synthetic vesicles segregated DNA-bearing beads into both daughters at a rate of approximately 82% (n=11).
results.detail: Division required externally imposed osmotic pressure and laser irradiation. The DNA was attached to beads, and the experiment did not demonstrate autonomous division.
results.quote:
With the ParMRC system, the bead segregation rate is ~82% (
n
= 11).

results.finding: PURE synthesized 36 non-ribosome proteins in one reaction and reconstituted protein expression; functional assays used 2 technical replicates.
results.detail: The experiment reconstituted a second-generation system after external purification, using supplied ribosomes. It did not demonstrate repeated regeneration of the full transcription and translation machinery; regeneration efficiency was insufficient for sustained self-regeneration.
results.quote: Finally, we show that all 36 non-ribosome PURE proteins can be synthesized simultaneously in a single PURE reaction and, after purification, can reconstitute a functional PURE system.

results.finding: Cell-free co-regeneration of EF-Tu and IF3 continued for up to 20 rounds; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The system regenerated two translation factors, but the text does not report regeneration of the full transcription and translation machinery.
results.quote: We further extended this framework to the co-regeneration of multiple translation factors and demonstrated sustainable co-regeneration of EF-Tu and IF3, another major essential translation protein, for up to 20 rounds.

results.finding: Cell-free PURE system regenerated T7 RNAP and two aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases for 20–25 hours; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The microchemostat repeatedly replaced reaction volume, but supplied ribosomes and other machinery. Regeneration of all transcription and translation machinery was not demonstrated.
results.quote:
Increasing DNA concentrations and maintaining 1:1
DNA template concentration ratios ultimately led to successful
regeneration lasting 20–25 hours (Fig. 4a, Supplementary Fig. 20).

results.finding: All 20 AARS were sustainably regenerated across up to 20 serial-dilution cycles in PURE, maintaining translation activity.
results.detail: Regeneration covered the 20 AARS, a subset of translation machinery; ribosomes, tRNAs, and other PURE components were supplied, and transcription machinery was not regenerated. Thus only part of m4 is demonstrated.
results.quote: After these improvements, we succeeded in the sustainable regeneration of all 20 AARS for up to 20 cycles of 2.5-fold serial dilutions.
